# Shipment Process Clause

Coordinates shipment booking, cancellation and delivery-address change requests, with shared action conditions and an explicit source-readiness guard. Accepting a request records an intention; only carrier responses establish shipment outcomes.

## Requests and readiness

All three actions require a nonempty text `requestId`. `requestAddressChange` also requires a nonempty text `address`, the proposed delivery address.

- `requestShipment` records action `book`. For a new request, `/shipment/status` must be exactly `new`; otherwise it fails with `SHIPMENT_ALREADY_REQUESTED`. It sets the status to `requested` and emits `Shipment Requested`.
- `requestCancellation` records action `cancel` and emits `Shipment Cancellation Requested`.
- `requestAddressChange` records action `address` and emits `Shipping Address Change Requested`.

New cancellation and address-change requests require status `requested` or `accepted`; otherwise they fail with `SHIPMENT_NO_LONGER_EDITABLE`. Neither changes the shipment status or `/destination` merely by being requested.

Before `requestShipment` runs, either `/clauses/documentSources` must be absent or `/sourceLinks/ready` must equal Boolean `true`. When the source clause exists, missing readiness does not satisfy this guard. Failure produces `SHIPMENT_SOURCES_NOT_READY`. This additional guard does not apply to the other two actions.

Each accepted new request is stored under its `requestId` in `/shipment/requests`, with `action`, the complete `input`, and an initially empty `responses` dictionary. The emitted event contains that input as `details`, the `requestId`, and `shipmentId` from `/instanceKey`.

Reusing a `requestId` with exactly the same action and input returns `duplicate` without another request event or state change. Different action or input produces `SHIPPING_REQUEST_ID_CONFLICT`. Duplicate detection precedes shipment-status checks, but follows connection and action guards. `acceptedNew` means the request was newly recorded, not that the carrier accepted it.

## Connections and conditions

`bindings` associates action names with dictionaries of named connections. No default trigger or requesting party is established for this type. Connections select their source through `on`: `workflow`, `channel`, `event`, `embedded`, `collection`, `change`, `initialized`, `activated`, or `timer`. Workflow connections require an authenticated `channel` or `party`; their existence alone does not establish any particular person's permission or obligation.

Connection `params` supplies action input. `when` defaults to `true`; a false condition skips execution. `parameters.conditions` adds a condition by exact action name, defaulting to `true` when omitted; failure produces `ACTION_CONDITION_FAILED`. Unknown action names in this dictionary are rejected. These conditions cannot bypass the shipment-readiness guard.

`before` runs after guards and before the action body. `after` runs only for `acceptedNew`. `once` defaults to `false`; when enabled, a completed new execution marks the connection as fired and suppresses later execution. A duplicate does not run `after` or consume `once`.

Path-based connections use non-root JSON Pointers. `embedded` and `collection` sources include embedded processing unless `embed` is `false`. Timer connections use either an absolute `timestamp` in Unix microseconds or `afterEvent` with positive integer `delayMs`. Relative timers default to `policy: first`; `latest` allows replacement by later triggers. `cancelOn` requests cancellation of the pending timer. Timer firing invokes an action; it does not confirm shipment.

Clause, action and connection names must be nonempty and contain no dot, slash or tilde. Changing an installed connection configuration requires a new clause key.

## Shipment state and carrier outcomes

All paths refer to the document where this clause executes, including a nested document's own state. `/shipment/status` is the recorded lifecycle state, not a configuration default: an absent status does not mean `new`. `/shipment/requests` retains requests and their responses keyed by outcome.

The shared response logic requires `call/channel` to equal `carrier` and a `requestId` identifying an existing request. Booking responses belong to `book` requests; cancellation and address responses must match their respective request actions.

Carrier acceptance or rejection requires `requested`; dispatch requires `accepted`; delivery requires `dispatched`. These outcomes set status to `accepted`, `rejected`, `dispatched` or `delivered` and emit the corresponding shipment event. `failed` has no additional predecessor-status guard beyond the terminal-state rule. The terminal statuses are `delivered`, `cancelled`, `rejected` and `failed`; a different subsequent outcome is rejected.

Confirmed cancellation sets status to `cancelled`. Confirmed address change writes the request's stored `input.address` to `/destination` while preserving status. Both confirmations require `requested` or `accepted`. `cancellationRejected` and `addressRejected` preserve status and do not share that editability guard, though terminal-state restrictions still apply. Cancellation and address requests permit only one distinct response.

An identical repeated response for the same request and outcome is a no-op before lifecycle checks; differing input conflicts. Responses record optional carrier `reason` and `trackingId`. An omitted `trackingId` preserves the stored identifier, falling back to an empty string if none exists; response events use empty strings for omitted `trackingId` and `reason`.

Carrier response functions are supplied, but this clause declares only the three request actions; response connection wiring is not established here.
